reasons: The fix option does nothing despite its help text.
Some pixel values and multi-line comments are not handled correctly.

terms.meaning: a named design setting, such as a color or size, that code refers to by name
a raw color or size typed directly into code instead of using a named token
a pattern written in symbols that matches text, used here to find colors and sizes
a number a program returns when it finishes; 0 means success and any other number means a problem
a color written as a hash sign followed by letters and digits, such as a red code
a size measured relative to the base font size, so it grows with text settings
a program that runs JavaScript outside a web browser

depends_on: Node.js built-in file and path modules

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loading tools and describing usage
sections.what: Loads the built-in file and path tools and describes how to run the script with a folder name.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard setup for a script that reads folders of source files.

sections.name: parseArgs
sections.title: Reading command options
sections.what: Reads the folder to scan, extra folders to ignore, the fix option, and the help option. Help prints the list of checks and stops the program.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the script run on different folders with extra ignores from the command line.
sections.watch_out: The `--fix` option is stored but never used anywhere in the script, so it has no effect despite its help text.

sections.name: patterns
sections.title: The list of value checks
sections.what: Lists the four kinds of hardcoded values the script looks for: hex colors, rgb colors, pixel sizes, and rem sizes. Each check has a message and a suggested replacement.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each check and its advice together so reports stay consistent.
sections.watch_out: The pixel check needs a colon before the number and at least two digits, so values such as 4px or values written without a colon are missed.

sections.name: extensions
sections.title: File types scanned
sections.what: Names the file types the script reads: style sheets, component files, and script files for several frameworks. HTML files are not on this list.
sections.why: Likely reason: targets style and component code, where tokens should be used.
sections.watch_out: HTML files are not checked here and need the separate HTML checker.

sections.name: skipPatterns
sections.title: Files skipped on purpose
sections.what: Lists file name patterns the script ignores: minified files, the Tailwind config, the global style file, and token definition files. These files are expected to hold raw values.
sections.why: The comments say the global style and token files are where values are defined, so they are skipped.
sections.watch_out: The patterns match any part of the full file path, so a file such as old-tokens.css is skipped too.

sections.name: getFiles
sections.title: Collecting files from folders
sections.what: Walks through a folder and all its subfolders, collecting files of the allowed types and skipping folders with ignored names.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the script scan a whole project tree automatically.
sections.watch_out: Ignored folder names match at any depth, so a folder named build anywhere in the tree is skipped.

sections.name: shouldSkip
sections.title: Checking the skip list
sections.what: Returns true when a file path matches any skip pattern, so the main loop moves past that file.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the skip decision in one small place.
sections.watch_out: Because it tests the full path, a folder name inside the path can cause a file to be skipped.

sections.name: scanFile
sections.title: Checking each line of a file
sections.what: Reads a file line by line, skips lines that start with comment markers, and records each hardcoded value with its line number, column, and a short piece of the line. Plain black and white hex colors are allowed.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The related tests say an earlier version skipped any line using a token, which this version does not do.
sections.watch_out: Only lines that start with a comment marker are skipped, so values inside a multi-line comment are still reported.

sections.name: formatReport
sections.title: Writing the printed report
sections.what: Builds the report text: a clean message when nothing is found, or otherwise a list by file showing line, found value, suggestion, and context, followed by counts by type.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes results easy to read and act on.
sections.watch_out: The context text is cut to 80 characters, so the found value may not be visible on very long lines.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Running the scan and setting the exit code
sections.what: Checks that a folder was given and exists, scans its files while skipping ignored ones, prints the report, and exits with a failure code if anything was found.
sections.why: Likely reason: a failure code lets automatic checks stop when hardcoded values appear.
sections.watch_out: The folder is resolved from the current working folder, so running from a different place can change which files are checked.

summary: A command-line checker that scans style and component source files for hardcoded colors and sizes that should use shared design tokens, and reports each one it finds.
purpose: Keeps the design system consistent by flagging raw values that should come from the shared token set.
why: The help text says it finds hardcoded values that should use design tokens. Likely reason for the failure exit code: lets automatic checks fail when violations appear.
how: 1. Read the command options. 2. Walk the chosen folder and collect matching files. 3. Skip ignored folders and token definition files. 4. Check each line for colors and sizes. 5. Print a report grouped by file, with a count summary. 6. Exit with a failure code if anything was found.
inputs: The folder to scan, extra folder names to ignore, the fix option (which does nothing), and the help option.
outputs: A printed report with line numbers, found values, suggestions, and counts, plus a success or failure exit code.
risks: Intentional values can be flagged as false alarms. Single-digit pixel sizes and values not placed after a colon are missed. Loose skip patterns can hide files. The fix option seems to work but does nothing.
debug: Run with the help option to confirm the options. If the folder is not found, check the path against the folder you are in. If a file is missed, check its extension and the skip patterns. If a value is flagged wrongly, check whether the line is a comment or sits inside a multi-line comment.
